heroHeadline: US-Iran 'Decision Day' Passes Without Deal; 14-Point MOU Framework Emerges; Iran Says Not 'Imminent' but Markets Price In Hormuz Reopening — Colombia Election 6 Days Away
heroSubtitle: May 25, 2026 — Trump's self-declared decision day on whether to resume military strikes against Iran passed without a formal deal announcement. Iran's foreign ministry characterized the state of talks as 'a degree of understanding' rather than an imminent agreement, while Secretary of State Rubio said 'significant progress' had been made. Trump posted that the naval blockade 'will remain in full force' until a deal is 'certified and signed.' The 14-point memorandum of understanding framework has now emerged publicly via Axios: Phase 1 would open the Strait of Hormuz within 30 days and allow Iran to freely sell oil; Phase 2 would be a 60-day window for nuclear program negotiations and sanctions relief. Oil markets are pricing in a near-term deal with prices falling in anticipation. Pakistan's Army Chief General Asim Munir continues as key intermediary. Trump called leaders across the Gulf, Pakistan, Turkey, and Israel on May 25 suggesting deal finalization push. NPR described the situation as 'a deal emerging, while war threats still loom.' In Colombia, with the election 6 days away (May 31), De la Espriella has surged to approximately 32.9% — making him a credible second-place finisher in the first round. With no candidate near 50%, a runoff on June 21 is virtually certain. The race now has three viable contenders: Cepeda (~44%), De la Espriella (~32.9%), and Valencia (~14-17%). The peace architecture — ELN talks, JEP, Total Peace — hangs on the result. Ukraine remains in a stalled phase: Zelensky on May 25 reiterated that 'Ukrainians are not ready to give away their land,' maintaining the Crimea and Donbas red lines that make the structural gap with Russia unbridgeable near-term. Lebanon is on Day 9 of its 45-day ceasefire extension; the Pentagon security track opens May 29.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN, African Union, IGAD, Crisis Group, USIP, PA-X Database, and Tier 1–3 sources across all media poles.
